nodes.label: Southern Lanka Capability Register
nodes.rationale: A consolidated production capability view for the Southern Lanka / CareCode tenant, compiled from the implemented application rather than from specification documents. Modules are listed in dependency order because each relies on the data and permissions established by the one above it.

nodes.label: Module 01 - Tenant and Multi-Company Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Employee-to-hierarchy mapping is a single mapping that drives every downstream scope: who appears on a roster, whose attendance a manager can open, and where a leave request is routed. Department deletion is a recoverable soft delete, never a permanent erase.

nodes.label: Domain-Resolved Data Isolation
nodes.rationale: The database is selected per request from the hostname, so no Southern Lanka record is readable from another tenant's domain and no rebuild or separate deployment is needed.

nodes.label: Cross-Tenant Administrator Mirroring
nodes.rationale: Active super administrators are mirrored into every tenant database so they can sign in and administer any organisation, with safeguards preventing a mirrored account from overwriting a real employee record.

nodes.label: Module 02 - Users and Role-Based Access
nodes.rationale: Roles are configuration, not code: administrators create job titles, tick capabilities and place the role in the approval hierarchy from inside the application with no release required.

nodes.label: Granular 38-Switch Capability Model
nodes.rationale: Thirty-eight independent switches gate every page and action, with separate read-only capabilities beside manage capabilities so a role can be given visibility without edit rights. The System Administrator role implies every management capability so a newly added capability never has to be granted retroactively and an administrator can never be locked out by an incomplete role registry.

nodes.label: Role-Tree Approval Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Each role names its parent; ancestors, descendants and peer lines are resolved from that tree to decide who may approve whom, with cycle protection when a role is re-parented.

nodes.label: Per-Employee Attendance Method Policy
nodes.rationale: Each employee is explicitly permitted to mark attendance by fingerprint terminal, by mobile application, or both. Records predating the policy are shown as 'Not set' rather than silently assumed.

nodes.label: Module 03 - HOD Scope and Reporting Lines
nodes.rationale: Head of Department is a role, but the departments a person heads are assigned individually; that assignment is the boundary for everything a HOD can see and approve and it is enforced when data is loaded, not merely hidden in the interface.

nodes.label: Strict HOD Scope Resolution (no fallback)
nodes.rationale: A HOD role with no departments assigned resolves to no access - never to 'sees everything' - and the scope never falls back to the person's own home department, which is where they sit rather than what they manage. Employee lists, attendance records, roster assignments and stored monthly summaries are filtered as they load so out-of-scope staff are never held in the session at all.

nodes.label: Leave and Overtime Approval Routing
nodes.rationale: A request fans out to every active Head of Department covering the applicant's department plus every approving tier above them in the role tree. A HOD is never an approver of their own request - it escalates upward instead. Attendance corrections route to the covering HOD, falling back to the nearest approving tier rather than broadcasting to every approver.

nodes.label: Module 04 - Shift Definition and Scheduling Engine
nodes.rationale: Shifts are defined once and reused across departments; rostering is a calendar grid of employees against dates supporting split days, back-to-back duty, midnight-crossing shifts, recurring weekly patterns and bulk spreadsheet import.

nodes.label: Overnight Shift Handling (end <= start crosses midnight)
nodes.rationale: Treated consistently across assignment, overlap detection, hour totals and attendance scoring, and labelled with a next-day marker so it is never misread as an earlier same-day time.

nodes.label: Holiday Classification Stamped at Assignment
nodes.rationale: Poya, Public and Mercantile classification is stamped onto the assignment when it is made so that editing the holiday list later never retroactively changes what a past roster recorded.

nodes.label: Recurring Weekly Roster Patterns
nodes.rationale: A pattern writes ordinary roster entries on a rolling horizon, extended weekly by a scheduled job, so every existing view and report reads it unchanged. The engine only ever touches entries it created - a hand-placed shift on the same date is left alone.

nodes.label: Bulk Roster Import with Review Step
nodes.rationale: Shift names are matched case-insensitively against the department's registered shifts; anything unrecognised is flagged rather than guessed, and nothing is written until the reviewer confirms.

nodes.label: Module 05 - Attendance and Real-Time Roster Engine
nodes.rationale: A monthly attendance matrix scored against each employee's actual rostered shifts rather than a fixed clock-in cutoff; anything implausible is flagged for a supervisor rather than silently corrected.

nodes.label: Fingerprint and Mobile Capture in One Record
nodes.rationale: Terminal punches are written into the same attendance sessions the mobile application uses so they appear immediately in every existing report with no separate reconciliation; each punch shows its own source badge for check-in and check-out independently.

nodes.label: Terminal Integration Safeguards
nodes.rationale: Idempotent per scan, debounced against duplicate punches, device and employee validated, coded errors returned; a rejected scan is not locked in so an offline terminal's retry queue still succeeds once the underlying issue is fixed.

nodes.label: Contiguous Duty Merging and Split-Day Separation
nodes.rationale: Same-day shifts that meet with a zero-minute gap merge into one duty block anchored at the first start and last end, so a missing punch between back-to-back shifts is never counted as a late arrival or early departure. Shifts with a real gap stay separate blocks scored on their own, and the gap is never counted as working time.

nodes.label: Shortfall Calculation Against the Roster
nodes.rationale: Late minutes run from the block's scheduled start to the actual check-in and early departure from the actual check-out to the block's scheduled end; both floor at zero so arriving early or staying late never offsets a shortfall elsewhere. Monthly totals are persisted as a stable figure for HR - the screen reports and never deducts pay or leave on its own.

nodes.label: Raw Punches Are Never Rewritten
nodes.rationale: Original timestamps are preserved exactly as captured and interpretation lives in a separate layer that allocates a session into rostered and unverified-extra time, so the audit trail of what the terminal actually recorded stays intact.

nodes.label: Exception Review Workflow and Open-Session Monitor
nodes.rationale: Implausibly long sessions, sessions reopened after a missed check-out, and sessions split by a back-dated roster change raise a review item moving flagged -> in review -> resolved. A scheduled job runs every fifteen minutes and only ever raises a review - it never closes a session or truncates recorded hours.

nodes.label: Recalculation on Retrospective Roster Change
nodes.rationale: Back-dating, editing or removing a roster entry queues a recalculation for that employee and date range so attendance interpretation stays consistent with the roster it is scored against.

nodes.label: Register Scope and Exclusions
nodes.rationale: Payroll is implemented for Southern Lanka but excluded by request and summarised separately; leave management appears only where it touches HOD routing and roster overlays; the Suspense module is built but switched off for this tenant; working patterns are designed but not yet built and tracked as planned work.
